# Authority and evidence hierarchy

Use current repository code, tests and serialization first; Accepted ADRs and
normative specifications second; then sealed G9U0/R1/R2/R3/R4/R5, G9X1 and G9P
evidence. Generated screenshots, packages and summaries are evidence only.

Before design or code, inspect the application-profile schema/compiler,
`AppGeoCeDG`, Desktop menu/controller/layout code, RuntimeFeatureService,
resource and provenance manifests, Windows packaging, the host Kernel
Continuity setting and XML/preferences lifecycle, the Advanced-settings UI,
the R3 public inspector, R4 selector/token authority and R5 ordinary transform
routes. Stop if these seams materially differ from their sealed authority.

The existing host `Kernel` Continuity option is the only continuity authority.
Reverify its setter, XML/preference readers and writers, default value and
Desktop settings control rather than creating a second setting.

# Scope

Implement application-profile schema version 2, deterministic version-1
migration, one manifest-owned action registry, named workspaces, views/docking,
bottom input and contextual help, toolbar/menu groups, maturity and feature
availability, localization, accessibility, workspace preferences, saved-layout
policy and workspace switching.

The default CeDG Construction workspace is professional and non-minimal. The
manifest/action registry must represent at least these families:

1. Inspect and construct;
2. Linear geometry;
3. Parameters and drivers;
4. Relations and intersections;
5. Circles, conics and curves;
6. Locus V2;
7. Metrics and validation;
8. Transformations and manual projections;
9. CeDG procedures and developments placeholders under independent gates;
10. Presentation and document; and
11. Automation and import/export.

Grouping and overflow are allowed; loss of discoverability is not. Stable
action IDs, localization/help, icons, feature requirements and unavailable
policy all come from the single manifest/action registry. Do not restore a
second hard-coded toolbar or menu authority.

Workspace membership changes presentation and discoverability only. It does
not alter command semantics, kernel truth, runtime feature policy or document
identity. Preserve the R3-fixed GeoCeDG menu lifecycle and the sole Locus V2
public opt-in. Do not introduce an intersection- or transformation-specific
runtime flag.

## Deterministic product policy

For the GeoCeDG CeDG Construction product, enforce the existing host setting:

```text
Continuity = OFF
```

This is a product invariant, not a workspace preference. It wins over prior
preferences, restart, workspace switching, restored profile/window state and
loading `.cedg` or compatibility `.ggb`. Use the existing Kernel setter and
serialization seam; add no second field. The settings UI must omit/disable the
on choice or expose the policy read-only. GeoCeDG Classic retains upstream
configurability and its isolated preference behavior.

Deterministic current semantic selection remains authoritative over continuity
heuristics. Ordinary regular behavior should be continuous when the same
current selector remains uniquely valid; genuine ambiguity fails closed. The
frontend must never use coordinates, proximity, list order, marker order,
screen state or movement history as solution identity.

## Free-input compatible redefine UX

Investigate and implement the bounded GeoCeDG product UX that lets an ordinary
free-input assignment such as `k=0.25` update the explicitly intended existing
compatible numeric object through the approved G9A compatible-redefine
transaction seam. This is a prospective G9U1 requirement only. The current
G9A `REDEFINE_CONTEXT_MISSING` rejection characterized during G9U0-R5 is not an
R5 semantic failure, and this requirement does not block the independently
authorized G9S1 phase.

A label may be used only to locate the explicitly intended current object in
the user-command context. It is never durable identity and must not become a
general label-based identity-inference mechanism. Preserve durable identity
only when the existing G9A compatibility predicate accepts the replacement and
the approved atomic transaction completes. An incompatible replacement follows
the existing new-identity semantics; an ambiguous or nonexistent intended
target fails closed. Do not infer compatibility or identity silently from a
matching label.

Characterize the actual Algebra/free-input route before code, including its
interaction with the normal existing-object Algebra-row edit. Validate atomic
failure, undo/redo, save/reopen and the resulting dependency/identity graph.
Characterize GeoCeDG Classic separately and preserve its approved compatibility
behavior rather than applying the GeoCeDG product policy globally. Do not
rewrite accepted historical G9A reports or weaken the G9A transaction and
compatibility authorities.

## Rich intersection presentation and materialization

Use this flow:

```text
Intersect(L,T)
 -> deterministic rich result remains semantic authority
 -> transient markers for the active/selected result only
 -> marker selection returns an existing current exact kernel token
 -> explicit create-one, create-selected or create-all materializes points
 -> optional explicit auto policy performs one visible frontend transaction
 -> later kernel recomputation creates no new GeoPoint
```

Markers default ON for the active-result context and exist only for current
finite solutions with truthful presentation evidence. Distinguish eligible and
nonmaterializable candidates accessibly without color alone. Stale,
overlap-only, dormant, quarantined or otherwise non-current evidence has no
selectable marker. Markers are presentation overlays: no GeoElement, XML, DAG,
Construction Protocol, undo state, durable ID or semantic revision.

Marker hit testing and UI proximity may choose among already published exact
tokens only. The frontend may not calculate, renumber or persist R4 intrinsic
phase/rank, adaptive phase cells/tubes or topology certificates. A transient
`Solution 1` label is presentation only.

The inspector remains open for repeated materialization unless explicitly
closed. It identifies already-materialized choices without exposing opaque
tokens as layout-sizing labels. Cancel creates nothing. Create-one creates one
ordinary exact-token GeoPoint. Create-selected and create-all-currently-eligible
create one point per exact current token, avoid duplicates and form one coherent
visible compound undo action.

Auto-materialization is an explicit, visible, opt-in frontend action over the
eligible-token snapshot immediately following an explicit Intersect action.
Auto OFF leaves the rich result with zero persistent child points. Recompute,
new root appearance, load/reopen, workspace switch and preference restoration
never create new DAG nodes.

Keep separate:

- kernel automatic reactivation of an already-existing materialized point when
  its same durable selector again resolves uniquely; and
- frontend materialization of a root that has never had a point.

Dormancy/reactivation changes definedness of the same GeoPoint and token; it is
not creation and triggers no frontend transaction.

G9U1 introduces no weaker `DETERMINISTIC_LOCAL` or certification policy.
Exact token means exact semantic identity, not exact arithmetic. Global
completeness and local point admissibility remain distinct.

## Post-R5 transformed Locus V2 contract

Expose the seven already implemented ordinary R5 command forms through the
same manifest/action registry:

- `Translate[L, v]`;
- `Rotate[L, angle]`;
- `Rotate[L, angle, center]`;
- `Reflect[L, point]` / ordinary point-mirror alias;
- `Reflect[L, line]` / ordinary line-mirror alias;
- `Dilate[L, factor]`; and
- `Dilate[L, factor, center]`.

Use the ordinary command families and the existing Locus V2 feature policy. Do
not add Locus-specific transform commands, mutable generic transform
interfaces, generic Path conformance, circle inversion or 3D forms.

Every transformed output is a new first-class semantic `GeoLocusV2` and must be
discoverable wherever a normal Locus V2 source is valid: semantic Point,
total/partial rich metric, rich intersection and further supported transforms.
The UI consumes the kernel result; it never transforms render samples.

For `Intersect(T(L), X)`, markers and materialization consume only current
selectors/tokens published by that transformed query's source-pair context.
Geometric covariance never transfers the source query's token, selector
phase/rank or current certificate. Transformed queries own new identities.
Require equivalent final bindings for direct, incremental, reverse and
save/reopen paths through the same regular final construction state.

For finite dilation `k=0`, retain the R5 Option-A semantic
`COLLAPSED_IMAGE`: source-valid domain, branches/components, parameter
authority and rich length zero remain; invalid source addresses remain invalid.
The displayed point image is not an isolated intersection root. Show no
selectable marker and materialize no point unless the kernel independently
publishes a current finite uniquely admissible exact token. Preserve truthful
overlap, non-isolated and unresolved diagnostics. Restoring nonzero scale
returns to ordinary current kernel authority without frontend migration.

Reflected and negative-scale loci preserve the R5 semantic parameter
orientation contract. Presentation orientation or screen order cannot replace
it. Composed transformed loci remain ordinary DAG compositions.

## Visual identity and author assets

Define a restrained professional GeoCeDG frontend identity through normal
application seams: application/window identity, reviewable accent/theme tokens,
workspace-indicating chrome, grouping/spacing, help/status, accessible contrast
and normal DPI/scaling. CeDG Construction must be distinguishable from the
GeoCeDG Classic diagnostic route without presentation becoming geometry.

Use two distinct stable logical roles:

- `geocedg.brand.topbar` for frontend/top-bar and product chrome only; intended
  author source `helixTopBar.png`;
- `geocedg.brand.startup` for startup/application identity and, only after
  suitability checks, deterministic window/package/file-association icon
  derivatives; intended author source `helixSnapshot.png`.

Do not assume a startup image is suitable at 16 x 16 or 32 x 32. For each
role, use `geocedg/resources/assets-manifest.yml` as the sole provenance
authority and record filename, SHA-256, dimensions, format/alpha, ownership,
license/review state, deterministic derivation tool/options and derived hashes.
Do not fabricate an absent asset, copy upstream branding or maintain duplicate
packaging copies. Keep an explicit bounded fallback and report the missing
author asset; a claimed final public branding/package PASS requires every asset
actually in claimed scope and author visual acceptance.

Classic remains visually identifiable as Classic and must not silently inherit
full CeDG Construction branding.

# Explicitly forbidden scope

Do not implement new geometry, intersection solving, token/identity semantics,
Locus metric semantics, R5 transform semantics, G9B, G9C, G9U2 or productive
G10. Do not add candidate markers to the kernel, turn transformed Loci into
render samples, introduce parallel commands or settings, fabricate branding,
or make presentation state geometric authority.

# Architectural placement

Workspace/profile/menu/marker/branding behavior belongs to application and
Desktop presentation. Kernel semantic truth remains in the already approved
R4/R5 authorities. Presentation switches, markers, hover, theme, icon,
workspace, zoom and DPI cause zero Construction, DAG, identity, semantic
revision, metric or intersection updates.

# Geometric invariants and degeneracies

Current finite, stale, unresolved, overlap, ambiguous, dormant, quarantined and
collapsed states remain exactly those published by the kernel. The frontend
must fail closed when current exact-token admissibility is absent. Genuine
topology and periodic seam/monodromy transitions may suppress a marker or leave
an existing point undefined; no UI heuristic may repair or conceal that state.

# Compatibility and serialization

`.cedg` remains native GeoCeDG document identity and `.ggb` compatibility
input. Retain ZIP/XML and `app="classic"`; do not infer semantics from filename.
Markers and product chrome have no document geometry. Existing exact-token
points, transformed loci and downstream dependencies retain their sealed
save/reopen/copy/undo contracts.

The retained risk
`G9-R4-PERIODIC-QUARANTINE-NATIVE-ROUNDTRIP` must be revisited in G9U1
persistence validation. Do not claim the missing native quarantine round trip
without new evidence; resolve or obtain explicit author disposition no later
than global G9 closeout.

GeoCeDG Classic opens and preserves supported `.cedg` without gaining
experimental creation authority. External upstream open of unknown GeoCeDG
types remains unsupported; no lossy downgrade is introduced.

# Stop conditions

Stop before or during implementation if:

- R5 is not sealed `PASS — AUTHOR APPROVED`, this exact prompt is not
  separately authorized, or entry authority/hash is dirty or inconsistent;
- UI exposure needs parallel transform commands, generic mutable transforms or
  generic Path conformance;
- frontend code would calculate/transfer selector identity, reuse a source
  query token or use order/coordinates/proximity/history as identity;
- collapsed-image UX would fabricate an isolated point, marker or token;
- marker UX cannot remain a transient consumer of current kernel authority;
- dormancy/reactivation would create a new point;
- Continuity OFF cannot use the existing host seam without a duplicate setting
  or Classic regression;
- free-input compatible redefine would require label-derived durable identity,
  bypass the G9A compatibility predicate/atomic transaction, or weaken
  ambiguous/nonexistent-target fail-closed behavior;
- theme, marker, icon or workspace state mutates Construction;
- asset provenance/licensing is unclear or an upstream asset would be copied;
- native `.cedg`, compatibility `.ggb`, Classic preservation, R5 semantics or
  any prior verification gate regresses; or
- completion would require G9B, G9C, G9U2 or productive G10.

Do not commit, push, merge, tag or self-approve unless a future author task
explicitly grants that action. Stop implementation at:

```text
G9U1 = IMPLEMENTATION CANDIDATE — PENDING AUTHOR REVIEW
selfApproved = false
authorApproved = false
passClaimed = false
```
